      pytest grabs stdin by default, so -s changes the behavior — though then your captured output ordering gets weird and that confuses the next debugging step.

      If the assert lives in a helper outside the test module, rewriting may not apply. I’d check where that function is defined and imported from.
    • in pre-commit hook passes locally, reformats in CI on same commit 2026-07-16
      Version drift is the first thing I'd suspect. Also check whether CI is running a different Python minor.
    • in capsys captures the test body but not output from a thread 2026-06-29
      There's also capfd, but if the thread already grabbed the old fd before the test started, that won't help either.
    • in parametrize gave two cases ids that look identical 2026-06-25
      If the dicts have a stable name key, that's usually enough. Otherwise you're stuck with the index and it gets ugly.
